sections.heading: Human diseases & microbial infections — the framework

blocks.text: Diseases split into **communicable (infectious — caused by pathogens, transmissible)** and **non-communicable (NCDs — lifestyle-genetic, non-transmissible: the growing majority of India's burden)**. Pathogens (in rising complexity): **viruses** (obligate intracellular — Covid, HIV, dengue), **bacteria** (TB, cholera, typhoid), **protozoa** (malaria, amoebiasis), **fungi** (candidiasis, mucormycosis), **helminths/worms** (soil-transmitted). **Transmission routes**: airborne/droplet (TB, Covid, flu), waterborne/faecal-oral (cholera, typhoid, hepatitis-A), vector-borne (malaria, dengue — mosquitoes), contact/blood/sexual (HIV, hepatitis-B), zoonotic (rabies, bird flu, Nipah).

rows: **Vaccination (immunisation), sanitation-safe water, vector control, hygiene, health education, nutrition**
Universal Immunisation Programme (Mission Indradhanush), SBM, safe-water
Screening, prompt diagnosis, treatment to prevent progression-transmission (DOTS for TB)
National One Health Mission, pandemic preparedness

items: **The double burden**: India fights communicable diseases (TB — the world's largest burden; vector-borne; diarrhoeal) AND a rising NCD tide (cardiovascular, diabetes, cancer — now ~65% of deaths) AND emerging/re-emerging threats (Covid, Nipah, drug-resistance) — the 'triple burden' framing.

**AMR — the silent pandemic**: antibiotic misuse (self-medication, agriculture, the Hyderabad-pharma-effluent hotspots) breeding resistance; India a global epicentre; the **National Action Plan on AMR** the response — an under-cited but high-value point.

**The prevention hierarchy is the answer**: primary prevention (vaccines-sanitation-vectors) is cheapest and most effective — India's immunisation, SBM and vector programmes embody it; the **health-environment correlation (ED-022)** underlies most infections.

**AP hook**: the Godavari-delta JE ecology (paddy-pig-mosquito), coastal vector-borne load, fluorosis (geogenic NCD), and Aarogyasri-family-doctor delivery — the state's disease-and-prevention profile.

glossary.definition: An infectious, transmissible disease caused by pathogens (virus, bacterium, protozoan, fungus, worm).
A non-transmissible chronic disease (cardiovascular, diabetes, cancer) — India's rising majority burden.
Preventing disease occurrence via vaccination, sanitation, vector control and education — the cheapest level.
Antimicrobial resistance — pathogens evolving to defeat drugs, the 'silent pandemic' of misuse.
A disease transmitted from animals to humans — the source of most emerging infections.
The shift of a population's disease burden from infectious to chronic non-communicable causes.

sections.heading: The four pathogen classes — a comparative primer

rows: TB (Mycobacterium), cholera (Vibrio), typhoid (Salmonella), tetanus, leprosy, pneumonia; **treated by antibiotics** (targeting bacterial machinery); AMR the growing threat
Obligate intracellular; hijack host cells; no independent metabolism
Covid, influenza, HIV, dengue, hepatitis, polio, measles, rabies; **antivirals limited; vaccines the mainstay** (viruses don't respond to antibiotics — the key public-health literacy point)
Malaria (Plasmodium), amoebiasis (Entamoeba), kala-azar (Leishmania), giardiasis; **anti-protozoal drugs** (chloroquine/ACT, metronidazole)
Candidiasis, aspergillosis, **mucormycosis ('black fungus' — the Covid-era surge)**, ringworm; **antifungals** (amphotericin, azoles)

blocks.text: **The treatment-logic distinction (the exam's core test)**: antibiotics work on BACTERIA only (not viruses) — the single most important public-health message against AMR; viruses need vaccines/antivirals; protozoa and fungi have their own drug classes. Diagnosis spans microscopy, culture, molecular (PCR), and immuno-assays (BN-035).

items: **The body's defence** (HB-043's file): innate (barriers, phagocytes, inflammation) + adaptive (antibodies, T-cells, memory) — vaccines train adaptive immunity; the pathogen-class matters for vaccine strategy (live-attenuated, inactivated, subunit, mRNA, vector).

**Control strategies by class**: bacterial (antibiotics + vaccines like BCG + sanitation), viral (vaccines + antivirals + isolation), protozoal (vector control + drugs + prophylaxis), fungal (antifungals + immune-status management) — control follows biology.

**AMR's cross-class shadow**: resistance now spans antibiotics (bacteria), antivirals, antimalarials (artemisinin resistance) and antifungals (azole-resistant candida) — the 'pan-drug-resistance' frontier; stewardship (rational use), new-drug pipelines, and surveillance the answers.
**AP hook**: TB-malaria-dengue load, mucormycosis during Covid, pharma-effluent AMR hotspots (region), and Aarogyasri treatment access — the state's infection-and-control profile.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The treatment-logic distinction (antibiotics = bacteria only) is this theme's anchor — state it explicitly; the four-class table with one example and one drug-class each is the complete factual spine.

prelimsPointers: **Bacteria** — prokaryotic, treated by antibiotics; **viruses** — obligate intracellular, need vaccines/antivirals (antibiotics don't work).
**Protozoa** — single-celled eukaryotes (Plasmodium-malaria, Entamoeba-amoebiasis, Leishmania-kala-azar).
**Fungi** — eukaryotic, often opportunistic; **mucormycosis ('black fungus')** surged in Covid's second wave.
**BCG** — the TB vaccine (bacterial); antibiotics target bacterial cell-wall/protein/DNA machinery.
**Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)** — first-line antimalarial; chloroquine resistance widespread.
**Amphotericin B, azoles** — antifungals; **AMR** now spans antibacterials, antimalarials and antifungals.
Diagnosis: microscopy, culture, **PCR (molecular)**, immuno-assays (ELISA/rapid).
mainsAngles: Antibiotics treat bacteria, not viruses — build the four-class pathogen primer around this treatment logic.

glossary.definition: A prokaryotic microorganism reproducing independently — treatable by antibiotics targeting its machinery.
An obligate intracellular pathogen hijacking host cells — countered by vaccines and antivirals, not antibiotics.
A single-celled eukaryotic parasite (malaria, amoebiasis) — treated with anti-protozoal drugs.
An infection exploiting weakened immunity (fungal mucormycosis) — status-dependent disease.
Rational, targeted antibiotic use preserving effectiveness — AMR's frontline defence.
Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy — the first-line antimalarial regimen against resistant Plasmodium.

sections.heading: The named diseases — a compact clinical-public-health table

rows: **ORS + zinc** (the life-saver), Rotavac vaccine, sanitation (SBM); the child-mortality killer historically
ORS/IV rehydration, oral cholera vaccine, safe water; epidemic-prone (Broad Street pump — epidemiology's birth)
**NTEP (National TB Elimination Programme)**, DOTS/BPaLM regimens, Ni-kshay portal; **India's 2025 elimination target** (ahead of SDG 2030); the world's largest burden
**NVBDCP → elimination by 2030**; ACT, bed-nets (LLINs), indoor spraying, RTS,S/R21 vaccines (Africa)
**NACO/NACP**, ART (free), prevention (condoms, PrEP), '90-90-90'→95 targets; India's concentrated-epidemic success story
JE virus (mosquito, pig-amplified); other AES causes
JE vaccine (UIP), vector control, the Gorakhpur/Godavari-delta relevance
Vector control (source reduction), no specific drug; dengue vaccines emerging; urban-monsoon surges
Culling, surveillance (One Health), pandemic-preparedness watch (mammalian-spread concern)

items: **The prevention-hierarchy applied**: waterborne (cholera-diarrhoea-typhoid) → sanitation-safe-water (SBM-JJM); vector-borne (malaria-dengue-JE-chikungunya) → source reduction + nets + spray; airborne (TB) → detect-treat-DOTS; blood/sexual (HIV) → prevention + ART — the ED-022 health-environment link made operational.

**India's elimination missions**: **TB by 2025** (ambitious, ahead of global), **malaria by 2030**, **kala-azar** (near-eliminated), measles-rubella, lymphatic filariasis — India as a disease-elimination laboratory; the ORS-and-vaccine revolution having already slashed child mortality.
**The One-Health emerging watch**: bird flu's mammalian spread, Nipah's recurrence (Kerala), Zika-Covid lessons — zoonotic surveillance the pandemic-prevention frontier.
**AP hook**: JE in the Godavari delta, coastal dengue-chikungunya surges, TB-HIV load, and the Aarogyasri-family-doctor delivery reaching these — the state's named-disease profile.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Group the eight named diseases by transmission route, then map each route to its control programme — that structure turns a disease list into a public-health strategy; the elimination-target dates are the currency facts.

prelimsPointers: **ORS + zinc** — the diarrhoea life-saver; **Rotavac** — indigenous rotavirus vaccine in UIP.
**TB**: **NTEP (National TB Elimination Programme)**; India's **elimination target 2025**; Ni-kshay digital portal; DOTS/BPaLM regimens.
**Malaria**: **NVBDCP**; **elimination target 2030**; ACT + LLINs + IRS; India cut cases sharply.
**HIV/AIDS**: **NACO/NACP**; free ART; India's concentrated epidemic largely controlled (95-95-95 goals).

**Dengue/chikungunya** — Aedes aegypti (day-biting); source reduction the main control; no specific antiviral.
**Bird flu (H5N1)** — zoonotic avian influenza; culling + One Health surveillance; mammalian-spread pandemic concern.
**John Snow's Broad Street pump (cholera, 1854)** — the founding of epidemiology.

glossary.definition: Oral Rehydration Solution — the glucose-salt therapy that made diarrhoea survivable; a public-health revolution.
Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course — the supervised-adherence strategy central to TB control.
National TB Elimination Programme — India's TB mission targeting elimination by 2025.
Reducing disease-carrying insects via source reduction, nets and spraying — the core anti-malaria/dengue tool.
Antiretroviral Therapy — the HIV treatment (free under NACO) suppressing viral load and transmission.
Reducing a disease to zero (or below-threshold) incidence in a defined area — India's TB/malaria/kala-azar goal.

sections.heading: Genetic engineering basics — the applied-biology view

blocks.text: (BN-034 covered impact-and-ethics; THIS note is the **mechanism primer** the health-biology unit wants.) The central dogma: **DNA → RNA → protein** — genetic engineering intervenes at the DNA level to change the protein output. The toolkit: **restriction enzymes** ('molecular scissors' cutting DNA at specific sequences — palindromic recognition sites), **DNA ligase** ('molecular glue'), **vectors** (plasmids, phages, cosmids carrying the insert into a host), **host cells** (E. coli, yeast, mammalian cells expressing the product), **selectable markers** (antibiotic resistance to identify transformants), and amplification/detection (**PCR, gel electrophoresis, blotting, sequencing**).

rows: Extract the gene of interest (and vector DNA)
Restriction enzymes cut both at matching sites (creating sticky/blunt ends)
DNA ligase joins insert into vector → recombinant DNA
Introduce recombinant vector into host (heat-shock, electroporation)
Markers + blue-white screening identify successful transformants
Host produces the target protein; downstream purification

items: **The gene-editing leap**: beyond cut-paste, **CRISPR-Cas9** edits the genome in place (guide-RNA targets, Cas9 cuts, cell repairs with the desired change) — precise, cheap, programmable; base/prime editing refine it further; ZFNs and TALENs were the precursors.

**Applications (the health-biology focus)**: recombinant pharmaceuticals (insulin, vaccines, clotting factors, growth hormone), gene therapy, diagnostics (probes, PCR), transgenic organisms (crops-HB-041, animals-HB-042), and industrial enzymes.

**The supporting techniques to name**: PCR (amplify), gel electrophoresis (separate by size), Southern/Northern/Western blotting (detect DNA/RNA/protein), DNA sequencing (read — Sanger to next-gen), hybridisation probes — the molecular-biology toolkit.
**AP hook**: recombinant-drug and vaccine manufacturing capacity (the region's pharma-biotech base), diagnostic labs, and Bt-cotton cultivation — genetic engineering applied in the state.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Name the toolkit precisely — restriction enzymes (scissors), ligase (glue), plasmid (vehicle), marker (label) — and walk the six-step workflow; that mechanistic literacy is exactly what the health-biology paper tests.

prelimsPointers: **Central dogma**: DNA → (transcription) RNA → (translation) protein.
**Restriction enzymes** cut DNA at specific palindromic sites (EcoRI the classic); **DNA ligase** joins fragments.
**Vectors**: plasmids, bacteriophages, cosmids, BACs — carry the insert into host cells.
**Selectable markers** (antibiotic resistance) + **blue-white screening** identify recombinants.
**PCR (Kary Mullis)** amplifies DNA; **gel electrophoresis** separates by size; **Sanger sequencing** reads.
**Blotting**: Southern (DNA), Northern (RNA), Western (protein).
**CRISPR-Cas9** (Nobel 2020) edits in place; **ZFNs, TALENs** the earlier editing tools; **recombinant insulin (1982)** the first product.

glossary.definition: The DNA→RNA→protein flow of genetic information — the framework genetic engineering intervenes in.
A protein cutting DNA at specific recognition sequences — genetic engineering's molecular scissors.
A DNA vehicle (plasmid, phage) carrying an inserted gene into a host cell for replication/expression.
A gene (often antibiotic resistance) letting researchers identify successfully transformed cells.
Polymerase Chain Reaction — the technique amplifying tiny DNA amounts exponentially.
The uptake of foreign DNA by a host cell (via heat-shock or electroporation) — the workflow's delivery step.
